title: Settings typing permission and mirror-input attention arming, proven under throttling
description: Add 'Allow typing from the Companion' to Settings > Companion (src/renderer/src/settings/sections/CompanionSettings.tsx, companion-settings.ts, companion-config-store.ts), default off, persisted in companion.json and shown in the section status. When main writes mirror input, notify the owning renderer with the PTY id and bytes over a new terminal event; the renderer's terminal runtime records it as terminal input so ADR-019 arming (recordInput in use-terminal-attention-controller.ts) happens for a phone-submitted Enter. No phone action clears attention. Add a smoke scenario in src/main/smoke that submits a prompt from a mirror while Away with the window hidden and background-throttled and asserts the next Ready and one Push.
acceptance_criteria: Toggling the permission persists and is reflected in the input route. A phone Enter arms Ready detection in the renderer exactly as a desktop Enter does. A mirror-submitted prompt yields Ready and one Push while Away under throttling in the smoke run. Viewing or typing from the phone never clears attention.

title: Phone page: ghostty-web terminal view with fit-to-width, on-screen keys, and input arming
description: In src/renderer/companion: render a selected live terminal with ghostty-web through the engine-neutral pane seam (src/renderer/src/terminal/terminal-pane.ts, ghostty-terminal-pane.ts) at the desktop's cols/rows, scaled to fit the phone width; never send resize. Add .wasm to the Companion asset allowlist (companion-assets.ts and companion-http.ts content-type maps) and 'wasm-unsafe-eval' to the page CSP in src/renderer/companion/index.html. Input starts disarmed: an explicit arm control enables typing, and it disarms on page hide, lease end, and inactivity. Provide on-screen keys for Enter, Escape, Tab, arrows, and Ctrl-C beside free text entry; send exact bytes to the input route. Replace the raw 'Transcript unavailable (reason)' text with the plain sentences the desktop uses in sessions-transcript-coordinator.ts.
acceptance_criteria: The wasm module loads from /assets on the phone page and a live terminal renders the tail then live output. The phone never sends a resize. Keystrokes are dropped client-side while disarmed and sent as exact bytes while armed; hiding the page disarms. Each on-screen key sends its documented byte sequence. Unavailable reasons render as plain sentences. Page tests cover arming, disarm on hide, and byte mapping.

title: Companion service and routes: one mirror lease per page over SSE and POST input
description: In CompanionSessionsService (src/main/companion/companion-sessions.ts), select on a row that is live, connected, and has a livePty opens a mirror lease on that instance under the page's companion demand owner; rows without a live hvir PTY keep the transcript path. One mirror per page; reselect replaces it. Add a terminal SSE event on /api/events carrying tail, bytes, and geometry, and POST /api/sessions/:handle/input that writes exact bytes under the lease with a bounded body. Input is refused unless the Settings typing permission is on. closePage, closeAll (revocation and shutdown), and PTY exit release the lease. Route table in companion-api-routes.ts; wire ports through companion-owner.ts and src/main/index.ts.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a live hvir terminal row streams its tail and live bytes to that page only. A second page selecting the same row gets its own mirror. Reselect, page close, revocation, and PTY exit each end the mirror and emit the matching event. Input route returns 403 when typing is disallowed in Settings and 409 when the lease ended or the instance changed; accepted bytes reach the PTY unchanged. Existing companion-sessions and companion-server tests keep passing.

title: PTY supervisor: retained output tail and a mirror lease door on an exact instance
description: Add tail retention to PtyStreamAttachment (src/main/pty/pty-stream-attachment.ts) that is independent of the renderer replay, which is consumed on attach; keep the same 256K char budget. Add PtySupervisor.attachMirror(instanceId, handlers) beside the owner-gated attach: bound to the immutable instanceId, not the renderer owner, so it survives transferRendererSession. The returned lease exposes write(data) that goes through the supervisor bound to the instance and fails closed when the instance changed, the PTY exited, or the lease ended. Handlers receive the tail on attach, live data, the current cols/rows on attach and on every resize, and exit. A mirror never resizes, kills, spawns, or transfers. Bytes are never logged or written to diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A mirror attached after the renderer receives the retained tail then live bytes. Mirror survives a renderer document transfer and ends on PTY exit. write through an ended lease, a mismatched instance, or an exited PTY throws and writes nothing. Resize from the renderer reaches the mirror as geometry; the mirror cannot resize. Tests at the supervisor altitude cover each fail-closed case.

title: ADR-050: The Companion mirrors a live hvir terminal and carries its user's keystrokes
description: Drafted at docs/adr/ADR-050-companion-live-terminal-mirror.md, indexed in docs/design.md, with a partial superseded-by notice on ADR-049. Uncommitted until the epic is approved. Decides: a mirror lease on an exact PTY instance as a second reader never a second owner; a retained output tail in the stream attachment; bytes cross uninterpreted and the phone emulates with ghostty-web at the desktop's geometry; phone keystrokes are exact user bytes bound to the instance, opt-in via Settings and per-mirror arming; attention classification stays in the renderer with no new clearing rule; eligibility equals the desktop's Interact.

title: Live terminal mirror and keyboard for hvir-owned sessions in the Companion
description:
## Motivation

The Companion (ADR-049) lists every session on the phone, and for a gas city row it
reads the transcript, answers the pending interaction, and sends a message. For a
terminal hvir launched itself it shows the row and refuses the transcript with
`not-projected`, because there is no supervisor API behind it.

That is nearly every session we run. Claude Code and Codex are started from a shell
inside an hvir terminal, and gas city workers are joined with `gc session attach`
inside an hvir terminal. On the desktop, Interact on such a row borrows the live
terminal pane with the whole keyboard. On the phone the same row is a dead end, and
the moment that matters most, a permission prompt or option picker waiting in
Claude Code's terminal UI, exists only on that screen. No transcript file carries it.

## What this epic does

A Companion page can select a live hvir-owned terminal row and see that terminal,
rendered on the phone by ghostty-web at the desktop's geometry, from a retained tail
of output onward. With typing allowed in Settings and armed on the page, keystrokes
return to that exact PTY instance. A prompt submitted from the phone still produces
the next Ready and the next Push, because the renderer keeps classifying. Nothing
changes on the desktop: one owner per PTY, no new clearing rule, no resize from the
phone.

Governing record: ADR-050, which partially supersedes ADR-049's exclusion of a
terminal screen and terminal input from the Companion.

## The seams, and why this is not an escalation

Main already sees every PTY byte. `PtyStreamAttachment` holds a set of data
listeners and fans output out to all of them; only the public door,
`PtySupervisor.attach`, is gated on the renderer owner and generation through
`requireOwned`. The replay buffer (`MAX_INITIAL_REPLAY_LENGTH`, 256 K chars) is
consumed when the renderer attaches, so a second reader gets nothing today; a
retained tail is the one new piece of state. Writes already go through
`PtySupervisor.write` under the same gate, so a mirror write is a second caller of
an existing authority bound to an instance rather than an owner.

The Sessions projection already carries the identity the mirror needs: a live row's
`livePty.handle` is the PTY `instanceId`, and its row handle is the PTY id. The
Companion sessions service already holds one demand owner per page
(`kind: 'companion'`), opens and closes pages on the SSE stream, and closes every
page on revocation. Mirror leases hang off that lifecycle.

The phone page is a second Vite entry served from the Companion's flat asset
bundle. ghostty-web loads its WebAssembly through a Vite `?url` import, so the
module is already emitted into that bundle. Two things block it on the phone today:
the asset allowlist in `companion-assets.ts` and `companion-http.ts` has no `.wasm`
content type, and the page CSP in `src/renderer/companion/index.html` lacks
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.

ADR-017, ADR-026, and ADR-032 forbid hvir composing text into a PTY. Phone
keystrokes are the user's exact bytes, uncomposed and unappended, bound to an exact
instance that fails closed on change. Those records are untouched.

## Decisions taken before decomposition

- Mirror, not transfer. The renderer stays the PTY's owner; the mirror is bound to
  the instance and survives a renderer document swap, ending only on PTY exit, page
  close, revocation, shutdown, or reselect.
- Bytes cross uninterpreted. Main keeps a tail and forwards; the phone emulates.
  No headless emulator in main.
- Geometry follows the desktop. The phone renders the desktop's columns and rows,
  scaled to fit, and never resizes the PTY.
- Typing is opt-in three times: a Settings permission defaulting to off, per-mirror
  arming on the page, and disarming on hide, lease end, or inactivity.
- Attention stays in the renderer. Main notifies the owning renderer of mirror
  input so ADR-019 arming happens where it always has. No phone action clears
  attention.
- Eligibility equals the desktop's Interact: live, connected, live PTY. External
  rows without an hvir terminal keep the transcript path.
- Transport reuses what exists: mirror output rides the page's SSE stream as a new
  event type; input rides bounded POST bodies. A socket is a later optimization,
  not a decision.

## Child issues

1. PTY supervisor: retained output tail and a mirror lease door on an exact
   instance. Tail retention in `PtyStreamAttachment` independent of renderer
   replay; `attachMirror(instanceId, handlers)` returning a lease with `write`,
   geometry on attach and on change, ending on exit; tests at the supervisor
   altitude including the fail-closed cases.
2. Companion service and routes: one mirror lease per page, `select` on an
   eligible live row opens it, a `terminal` SSE event carries tail, bytes, and
   geometry, `POST /api/sessions/:handle/input` writes under the lease, and
   page close, reselect, and revocation release it.
3. Phone page: terminal view in ghostty-web through the engine-neutral pane seam,
   `.wasm` in the asset allowlist and CSP, fit-to-width scaling, on-screen keys
   (Enter, Escape, Tab, arrows, Ctrl-C), arm and disarm controls, and the
   `not-projected` dead end replaced by the same plain wording the desktop uses.
4. Settings and attention: the typing permission in Settings > Companion with its
   status, the mirror-input notice from main to the owning renderer recorded as
   terminal input, and a smoke scenario proving a phone-submitted prompt yields
   Ready and Push while Away under background throttling.
5. Docs: operator runbook section for the mirror and typing permission, ADR index
   entries (already drafted with ADR-050), and the Companion COMPASS.

Order: 1 first; 2 and 3 in parallel on 1; 4 on 2; 5 last.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Selecting a live hvir terminal row on the phone shows that terminal's screen,
      including a Claude Code permission prompt that is on the desktop's screen
- [ ] The mirror survives a desktop reload of the renderer document and ends when
      the PTY exits, the page closes, or pairing is revoked
- [ ] With typing disallowed in Settings, no input route accepts bytes; with it
      allowed but unarmed on the page, no keystroke reaches the PTY
- [ ] An armed Enter from the phone answers a Claude Code prompt on the desktop,
      and the row leaves the actionable set when output resumes
- [ ] A prompt submitted from the phone produces the next Ready and one Push while
      Away, with the desktop window hidden and throttled
- [ ] The phone never resizes the PTY; the desktop's geometry is what the phone
      renders
- [ ] Mirror bytes never appear in logs, diagnostics, or push text
- [ ] Rows without a live hvir PTY keep their existing transcript or unavailable
      path, with a plain sentence instead of a reason code

title: Docs: runbook, ADR index, and Companion COMPASS for the terminal mirror
description: Extend docs/runbooks/companion-operator.md with the mirror and the typing permission, including the geometry and first-frame notes from ADR-050's consequences. Confirm the ADR-050 entry and the ADR-049 notice in docs/design.md. Update src/main/companion COMPASS (or create it) with the mirror lease lifecycle and the wasm allowlist gotcha.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook explains enabling typing, arming on the page, and what the phone shows for rows without a live PTY. design.md index and ADR-049 notice match the README's relationship-line shape. COMPASS names the mirror lease owner and the asset allowlist.
